summary: Dispatch liveness is event-driven: delete the 30-minute heartbeat-age reap; reap on pane death and idle-with-claim; a step owns its own budget; no restart from zero

options.description: Delete the heartbeat-age reap. The executor module publishes its state (turn running, background agent running, idle awaiting clear) to the board on its own events; pane death posts to dispatch and requeues at once; dispatch reaps idle-with-claim-and-no-verdict with no timer; the developer round carries a step-owned budget and reports iterate-needed keeping the worktree; nothing restarts a claim from zero. The state.json file stays as the lease-push claim binding. Amend RFC-0041 OQ-3 and RFC-0051 stall paragraph.
Keep the age rule; the executor module refreshes lastHeartbeat on every turn and subagent event. Keeps the 30-minute number and retry-from-zero.
Keep the stall detector as is; the planner refreshes heartbeats by hand for long rounds.

body: The stall detector (AISDLC-826, RFC-0041 OQ-3, RFC-0051 stall paragraph) reaps a claim whose inflight state.json lastHeartbeat is older than 30 minutes. The heartbeat is a step-transition stamp written only by next-step calls, never during a step, so a developer round longer than 30 minutes is indistinguishable from a dead executor. It reaped AISDLC-1209 at 2026-11-06T19:45Z mid-round and restarted it from zero; AISDLC-1210 was two minutes from the same. AISDLC-948 and AISDLC-1124 were earlier patches to the same proxy. Requirement questioned: a claim must be released when its executor is dead, wedged or finished. True signals already exist: tmux window gone (death), verdict written (finished), the executor module's turn.start/turn.complete events (busy), and the host tick already reads the first two. The 30-minute age and the retry-from-zero (limit 2) were never requirements of AISDLC-826, which asked for detection.
